_readme: Owned by Agent B (task B3b). Agent A wrote the two entries below as the §7 fallback
so A5 was not blocked; overwrite them freely, the assembler does not care.
Keys MUST be finding IDs from contract/types.ts FINDING_IDS. A snippet whose ID is
not in the generated project's appliedFindingIds is skipped, so it is safe to ship
snippets for findings that only some option combinations mitigate.
`body` lines are Solidity statements placed inside the test function at one indent.
`helpers` lines are emitted at contract level (extra helper contracts, constants).
Placeholders are substituted before emission; any {{UNKNOWN}} left over is a hard
error rather than a silently broken test.
A finding may have more than one snippet (e.g. one per preset). Key them
'<FINDING_ID>#<variant>'; everything before the '#' is the finding ID.

placeholders.{{CONTRACT}}: the deployed instance under test, e.g. `harness`
placeholders.{{CONTRACT_TYPE}}: the generated contract's type name, e.g. `MyFlashLoanReceiver`
placeholders.{{POOL}}: IPool, resolved from the addresses provider in setUp
placeholders.{{ATOKEN}}: the aToken for {{ASSET}}, resolved from the Pool in setUp (never hard-coded)
placeholders.{{PARAMS}}: call to `_defaultParams()`, which abi.encodes a valid FlashParams
placeholders.{{PARAMS_STRUCT}}: call to `_defaultFlashParams()`, the same params unencoded
placeholders.{{OWNER}}: the authorised caller created in setUp
placeholders._note: Snippets may declare `presets`; omitted means both. A snippet is emitted only if its finding ID is in appliedFindingIds AND its preset matches.
placeholders.{{ONE}}: 10 ** decimals of the asset, resolved on the fork in setUp
placeholders.{{AMOUNT}}: roughly a thousand dollars of the asset in raw units (1_000e6 for USDC, 0.25e18 for WETH); every amount in a snippet is a multiple or fraction of this so the suite is valid for any asset
placeholders.{{MORPHO}}: the Morpho Blue singleton address constant (Morpho preset only)
placeholders.{{COMET}}: the Comet address constant for {{ASSET}} (Compound preset only)
placeholders.{{TOKEN}}: the sale token instance deployed in setUp (token-sale preset only)

AAVE-FL-001.title: Flash-loan callback not gated to Pool + initiator

incidents.name: DODO MarginTrading
Mimo SuperVault (Code4rena H-02)

comments: AAVE-FL-001 — anyone may call Pool.flashLoanSimple naming OUR contract as the
receiver. Aave then invokes our callback on their behalf, with their params.
Checking msg.sender == Pool is NOT enough: the Pool really is the caller.
This is the bug that drained DODO MarginTrading and Mimo SuperVault.

AAVE-FL-002.title: Attacker-controlled calldata executed from callback params

incidents.name: Mimo SuperVault aggregatorSwap(dexTxData)

comments: AAVE-FL-002 — the tutorial pattern decodes `params` into (address target,
bytes data) and calls it, turning finding 001 from a revert into a drain.
Here `params` decodes to a fixed struct with no call target, so hostile bytes
cannot become an external call. Asserted even with both other gates satisfied.
body: // Worst case: the attacker somehow satisfies the caller AND initiator gates.

premium. The initiator gate is what stops it, so assert the balance survives.

incidents.name: PoolTogether AaveV3YieldSource (Code4rena H-01)

AAVE-RISK-006.title: LTV-0 aToken poison dust can freeze withdrawals

incidents.name: StErMi — Aave v3 LTV-0 bug bounty
ChainSecurity — Grove ALM zero-LTV review

comments: AAVE-RISK-006 — one wei of a zero-LTV aToken, sent by anyone, must not brick
redemptions. aTokens are ordinary transferable ERC20s, so this grief costs the
attacker a single wei and there is no permissionless way to push it back out.
The aTokens are acquired by genuinely supplying to Aave: aToken balances are
scaled, so a forged `deal` balance would not behave like a real transfer.
body: assertGt(received, 0, "1 wei of zero-LTV aToken bricked redemptions");

MRPH-VLT-016.title: Morpho assets/shares not mutually exclusive

incidents.name: Morpho Blue ErrorsLib.INCONSISTENT_INPUT

comments: MRPH-VLT-016 — supply and withdraw take BOTH an assets and a shares argument,
and exactly one must be zero. Setting both is not a rounding nuisance, it is a
hard revert: "inconsistent input". The vault names the zero rather than
passing a bare literal, so the intent is visible at every call site.
body: // The vault's own supply path is well-formed: a deposit lands.
// And this is what the malformed call does, straight to Morpho.
// marketParams() is itself a call, so it must be hoisted above expectRevert —
// otherwise the expectation binds to it instead of to supply().

MRPH-CB-017.title: Morpho callback not gated to the Morpho singleton

incidents.name: Morpho Blue IMorphoCallbacks
Same shape as the Aave callback bug that drained DODO

comments: MRPH-CB-017 — passing non-empty `data` to Morpho makes it call back into
this contract. An ungated callback is the same Critical that drained DODO on
Aave. The vault passes empty bytes and implements no callback at all, so
there is no entry point to gate and nothing to get wrong.
body: // No fallback and no callback: an unknown selector has nowhere to land.
assertFalse(ok, "vault exposes a Morpho callback an attacker could drive");
assertFalse(ok, "vault exposes a Morpho flash-loan callback");

MRPH-MKT-018.title: Market parameters not pinned at construction

incidents.name: Morpho Blue MarketParamsLib — a market IS the hash of its parameters

comments: MRPH-MKT-018 — Morpho identifies a market by the hash of five fields. A vault
that accepts them per call can be aimed at a market with a different oracle or
LLTV while every function signature stays identical. Pinning them as
immutables means the market cannot be repointed after deployment.
body: assertEq(p.loanToken, {{ASSET}}, "loan token drifted from the vault asset");
// There is no setter: nothing on the ABI can change any of these.
assertFalse(ok, "market parameters are mutable after deployment");

CMPD-VLT-019.title: Comet withdraw beyond the supplied balance opens a borrow

incidents.name: Comet withdrawBase: no amount <= balance check; NotCollateralized is the only guard
ChainSecurity Comet audit §5.1 — balances can go negative through the same path

comments: CMPD-VLT-019 — Comet.withdraw() has no "amount <= balance" check: past the supplied
balance it BORROWS, and it can, because supplyTo() lets anyone hand this vault a
collateral position without asking. The vault's limits and its withdraw gate must
hold even when its own book is wrong, so the book is corrupted on purpose here.
body: // Anyone can gift the vault collateral on Comet. No permission is needed for `dst`.
// Corrupt the book: the vault now believes it holds 100x its real position.
// The limit still reports the real position, not the book.
assertLe({{CONTRACT}}.maxWithdraw(alice), real, "maxWithdraw promised more than Comet holds");
// One wei past the position is refused; Comet would have borrowed it.

CMPD-VLT-020.title: Comet present-value rounding booked as the requested amount

incidents.name: Code4rena 2023-07 Reserve M-13 — Comet moves 1-10 wei more than asked

comments: CMPD-VLT-020 — Comet stores a principal and shows a present value; both conversions
round DOWN, so the balance after supplying X can be short of X by a base unit. A
vault that books X drifts above its real position and the last exit fails inside
Comet. Assert the book never exceeds the position and a full exit still works.
body: assertLe({{CONTRACT}}.totalAssets(), held, "book exceeds the Comet position");
assertGe({{CONTRACT}}.totalAssets() + 2, {{AMOUNT}}, "credited far less than was supplied");
// The last redeemer must be able to leave without underflowing inside Comet.
assertLt({{CONTRACT}}.totalAssets(), {{AMOUNT}} / 1_000, "dust left after a full exit");

LPAD-SALE-030.title: Raised funds withdrawable before the sale is finalized

incidents.name: BetaPresale (May 2025) — mutable recipient + instant forwarding, drained via a flash loan
PartyDAO (Code4rena 2023-04, H-03) — refunds insolvent after funds moved

comments: LPAD-SALE-030 — nothing leaves the sale before finalize() has run and succeeded, and
then only to the immutable treasury. There is no recipient setter to hijack and no
path for the owner to take the money early.
body: assertEq(address({{CONTRACT}}).balance, c, "ETH left the sale before it closed");
assertTrue({{CONTRACT}}.succeeded(), "soft cap met but sale did not succeed");
assertEq({{CONTRACT}}.TREASURY().balance - treasuryBefore, raised, "raise did not reach the treasury");

LPAD-SALE-031.title: Tokens claimable before finalization, or claimable twice

incidents.name: AISOTH Presale (June 2026) — buy and claim in one transaction, dump into the pool
vVv Launchpad (Sherlock H-1) — claim not bound to the claimant

comments: LPAD-SALE-031 — a claim before the sale has closed is a flash-arbitrage against the
pool; a claim that does not track what was already paid is a double claim.
body: assertEq(got, {{CONTRACT}}.allocationOf(alice), "claim paid less than the allocation");

LPAD-SALE-032.title: Push-based refunds / reentrancy in claim and refund

incidents.name: OpenZeppelin 2.x RefundableCrowdsale — escrowed, pull-based refunds
Decent Crescendo (Feb 2026) — ETH paid out before state was updated

comments: LPAD-SALE-032 — a refund is pulled by its owner, never pushed in a loop, and the
balance is zeroed before the ETH moves. A receive() that calls back in gets nothing.
body: assertEq(address(reenterer).balance, c, "refunded more or less than was contributed");
vm.expectRevert(bytes("refund failed")); // the sale said NothingToRefund; the wrapper reports it

LPAD-SALE-033.title: Hard cap or per-wallet cap not enforced

incidents.name: BetaPresale (May 2025) — per-sender cap recycled through 70 fresh contracts
PartyDAO (Code4rena 2022-09, M-02) — per-wallet caps are sybil-able

comments: LPAD-SALE-033 — every cap is checked on every contribution. The per-wallet cap is
friction rather than security (a second wallet is free); the hard cap is not.
body: // Fill the hard cap, then one more valid contribution is refused.

LPAD-SALE-034.title: Whitelist proof not bound to this sale (replayable)

incidents.name: vVv Launchpad (Sherlock H-1) — signed claim front-run by a stranger
Rova (Sherlock #421) — message without chainId replayable across networks

comments: LPAD-SALE-034 — the Merkle leaf is the caller, so a whitelisted wallet's proof is
worthless in anyone else's hands, and the root is this contract's alone.
body: // Alice's proof, presented by a stranger.
// And the root cannot be moved once the sale is open.

LPAD-SALE-035.title: Price / token-decimals mismatch in the allocation math

incidents.name: Rova (Sherlock #537) — payment-token units subtracted from sale-token units

comments: LPAD-SALE-035 — one price unit of ETH must buy exactly one whole token, whatever
the token's decimals are, and fractions must scale the same way.
body: assertEq(unit, 10 ** {{TOKEN}}.decimals(), "TOKEN_UNIT does not follow the token's decimals");
assertEq({{CONTRACT}}.tokensFor(price), unit, "one price unit must buy one whole token");
assertEq({{CONTRACT}}.tokensFor(3 * price + price / 2), 3 * unit + unit / 2, "fractions do not scale");

LPAD-SALE-036.title: Fee-on-transfer sale token breaks allocation accounting

incidents.name: Juicebox (Code4rena 2022-07, #304) — fee-on-transfer token booked at face value

comments: LPAD-SALE-036 — the sale books the tokens that actually arrived and refuses to
finalize as a success unless it holds every token it owes. An unfunded (or
under-funded, fee-on-transfer) sale fails and refunds instead of stranding claims.
body: assertFalse({{CONTRACT}}.succeeded(), "succeeded while holding none of the tokens it owes");
assertEq({{CONTRACT}}.refund(), c, "contributor could not get out");

LPAD-SALE-037.title: Vesting unlock math wrong at the cliff

incidents.name: Tokensoft (Sherlock M-2) — vesting rounding blocked claims

comments: LPAD-SALE-037 — nothing before the cliff, linear after it, everything at the end.
Pinned at the three boundaries so a refactor cannot move them.

assertEq({{CONTRACT}}.vestedOf(alice), 0, "the cliff itself must not release a lump");

and holders. A holder cannot pass tokens to another wallet and cannot seed the pair.

LPAD-CURVE-042.title: Buy/sell without a slippage bound or deadline

incidents.name: Virtuals Protocol (Code4rena 2025-04, M-02/M-03) — no minAmountOut, slippage computed at execution

comments: LPAD-CURVE-042 — a trade with no floor on output and no deadline is a free sandwich

LPAD-CURVE-043.title: Sell-side ETH refund reentrancy

incidents.name: Decent Crescendo (Feb 2026) — sell() paid ETH before updating the price

comments: LPAD-CURVE-043 — state is final and the tokens are in before any ETH leaves, under
a reentrancy guard. A receive() that sells again from inside the payout gets nothing.
body: assertEq(attacker.reentered(), 0, "sell() was re-enterable during the ETH payout");
assertEq(token.balanceOf(address(attacker)), held - held / 2, "the re-entrant sell went through");

LPAD-CURVE-044.title: Curve rounding favours the trader

incidents.name: USM/FUM (Aug 2026) — curve payout depended on how a sale was split
Uniswap V2 getAmountOut floors the output

comments: LPAD-CURVE-044 — every output is floored by rounding the residual reserve up, so a
buy followed by a sell can never return more than went in, at any size.
body: uint256[6] memory samples = [uint256(1), 3, 1e9 + 7, g / 1000, g / 7, g - 1];
assertLe({{CONTRACT}}.previewSell(tokensOut), samples[i], "round trip pays out more than it took in");
// Output is monotone in input: more ETH never buys fewer tokens.
// And on chain, after fees, the same holds for a real trade.
assertLe(back, wei_, "buy-then-sell returned more ETH than it cost");
